subject: maths
title: Mental Multiplication and Division
seo_title: Year 4 Mental Multiplication and Division Worksheets: × 0, × 1, Derived Facts and Factor Pairs
standard_text: Use place value, known and derived facts to multiply and divide mentally, including: multiplying by 0 and 1; dividing by 1; multiplying together three numbers; recognise and use factor pairs and commutativity in mental calculations.
meta_desc: Free Year 4 maths worksheets on mental multiplication and division: multiplying by 0 and 1, dividing by 1, derived facts like 60 × 7, multiplying three numbers and factor pairs. 100 questions with an answer key, matched to the National Curriculum.
key_big: Use a fact you know to work out one you don’t: 6 × 7 = 42, so 60 × 7 = 420.
key_sub: Any number × 0 is 0. Any number × 1 or ÷ 1 stays the same. Multiply three numbers in any order, and use factor pairs to split a hard calculation.
body_html:
Use facts you already know

You do not need a written method for every calculation. Use your times tables, place value and a few simple rules to work out harder facts in your head.

Multiply by 0 and 1, divide by 1

RuleExampleWhy
A number × 1 = the same number8 × 1 = 8One lot of 8 is 8
A number × 0 = 07 × 0 = 0Seven lots of nothing is nothing
A number ÷ 1 = the same number9 ÷ 1 = 9Put all 9 in one group

Use place value: derived facts

× 10 moves every digit one place to the left. So if you know 6 × 7 = 42, you also know 60 × 7 = 420.

Example

Work out 60 × 7 and 420 ÷ 7.

6 × 7 = 42. 60 is 6 tens, so 60 × 7 = 42 tens = 420. Use the inverse: 420 ÷ 7 = 6 tens = 60.

Answer: 420 and 60

Multiply three numbers

You can multiply in any order. Look for a pair that makes 10 or 20 first.

Example

Work out 2 × 7 × 5.

Swap the order: 2 × 5 = 10. Then 10 × 7 = 70.

Answer: 70

Factor pairs

A factor pair is two numbers that multiply to make a number. 3 × 8 = 24, so 3 and 8 are a factor pair of 24. The factor pairs of 24 are 1 × 24, 2 × 12, 3 × 8 and 4 × 6.

Example

Work out 15 × 6 using a factor pair.

6 = 2 × 3. So 15 × 6 = 15 × 2 × 3 = 30 × 3 = 90.

Answer: 90

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
7 × 0 = 7Anything × 0 is 0
8 ÷ 1 = 1Dividing by 1 keeps the number: 8 ÷ 1 = 8
60 × 7 = 42 or 4,20060 is 6 tens, so the answer is 42 tens = 420
2 × 7 × 5 = 35Use all three numbers: 2 × 5 = 10, then 10 × 7 = 70
Missing a factor pair of 24Test 1, 2, 3, 4 … in order until the pairs meet
Saying 8 + 16 = 24, so 8 and 16 are a factor pairA factor pair must multiply: 8 × 3 = 24

faq.q: What are mental multiplication and division strategies in Year 4?
faq.a: Pupils use times tables, place value and simple rules to calculate in their heads. For example, 6 × 7 = 42 tells you that 60 × 7 = 420, and 2 × 9 × 5 is easier as 2 × 5 = 10, then 10 × 9 = 90.

faq.q: What times tables should a Year 4 child know?
faq.a: By the end of Year 4, the National Curriculum expects children to recall all multiplication and division facts up to 12 × 12.

faq.q: What is the Multiplication Tables Check?
faq.a: It is a short online check taken in June of Year 4 in England. Children answer 25 times tables questions up to 12 × 12, with 6 seconds for each one.
Two numbers that multiply to make a given number. The factor pairs of 12 are 1 × 12, 2 × 6 and 3 × 4.

items.q: What is 8 × 1?
items.e: Multiplying by 1 keeps the number the same. 8 × 1 = 8. (One lot of 8 is 8.)

items.q: What is 1 × 6?
items.e: Multiplying by 1 keeps the number the same. 1 × 6 = 6. (One lot of 6 is 6.)

items.q: What is 1 × 12?
items.e: Multiplying by 1 keeps the number the same. 1 × 12 = 12. (One lot of 12 is 12.)

items.q: What is 157 × 1?
items.e: Multiplying by 1 keeps the number the same. 157 × 1 = 157. (One lot of 157 is 157.)

items.q: What is 7 × 0?
items.e: Multiplying by 0 always gives 0. 7 × 0 means 7 lots of 0, so there is nothing at all. Writing a 0 on the end is the rule for × 10, not × 0.

items.q: What is 0 × 9?
items.e: Multiplying by 0 always gives 0. 0 × 9 means 0 lots of 9, so there is nothing at all. Writing a 0 on the end is the rule for × 10, not × 0.

items.q: What is 11 × 0?
items.e: Multiplying by 0 always gives 0. 11 × 0 means 11 lots of 0, so there is nothing at all. Writing a 0 on the end is the rule for × 10, not × 0.

items.q: What is 0 × 245?
items.e: Multiplying by 0 always gives 0. 0 × 245 means 0 lots of 245, so there is nothing at all. Writing a 0 on the end is the rule for × 10, not × 0.

items.q: What is 8 ÷ 1?
items.e: Dividing by 1 keeps the number the same. Share 8 into 1 group and all 8 are in that group. 8 ÷ 1 = 8.

items.q: What is 12 ÷ 1?
items.e: Dividing by 1 keeps the number the same. Share 12 into 1 group and all 12 are in that group. 12 ÷ 1 = 12.

items.q: What is 60 ÷ 1?
items.e: Dividing by 1 keeps the number the same. Share 60 into 1 group and all 60 are in that group. 60 ÷ 1 = 60.

items.q: What is 314 ÷ 1?
items.e: Dividing by 1 keeps the number the same. Share 314 into 1 group and all 314 are in that group. 314 ÷ 1 = 314.

items.q: Find the missing number: ? × 9 = 9
items.e: Only 1 keeps the number the same: 1 × 9 = 9. 0 × 9 = 0 and 9 × 9 = 81.

items.q: Find the missing number: 12 × ? = 0
items.e: A product is 0 only when you multiply by 0: 12 × 0 = 0. 12 × 1 = 12.

items.q: Find the missing number: 25 ÷ ? = 25
items.e: Dividing by 1 keeps the number the same: 25 ÷ 1 = 25. 25 ÷ 25 = 1 and 25 ÷ 5 = 5.

items.q: Which calculation is correct?
items.e: Times 0 gives 0, so 6 × 0 = 0 is correct. 6 × 0 is not 6, 6 ÷ 1 is 6 (not 1), and 6 × 1 is 6 (not 7).

items.q: Which calculation is correct?
items.e: Dividing by 1 keeps the number: 9 ÷ 1 = 9. Anything times 0 is 0, in either order.

items.q: What is 6 × 8 × 0?
items.e: 6 × 8 = 48, then 48 × 0 = 0. If one of the numbers is 0, the answer is always 0.

items.q: What is 1 × 7 × 1?
items.e: 1 × 7 = 7, then 7 × 1 = 7. Multiplying by 1 never changes the number. (9 comes from adding.)

items.q: Which calculation has a different answer from the others?

sets.title: Use place value: × 10, × 100 and derived facts

items.q: What is 36 × 10?
items.e: × 10 moves every digit one place to the left: 3 tens become 3 hundreds and 6 ones become 6 tens. A 0 holds the ones place. 36 × 10 = 360.

items.q: What is 100 × 8?
items.e: × 100 moves the digit two places to the left: 8 ones become 8 hundreds. 100 × 8 = 800.

items.q: What is 45 × 100?
items.e: × 100 moves both digits two places to the left: 45 × 100 = 4,500. 450 is only × 10.

items.q: What is 10 × 70?
items.e: 70 is 7 tens. 10 × 7 tens = 70 tens = 700.

items.q: What is 420 ÷ 10?
items.e: ÷ 10 moves every digit one place to the right: 4 hundreds become 4 tens and 2 tens become 2 ones. 420 ÷ 10 = 42.
÷ 100 moves every digit two places to the right: 3,500 ÷ 100 = 35. 350 is only ÷ 10.

items.q: You know that 6 × 7 = 42. What is 60 × 7?
items.e: Use the fact 6 × 7. 60 is 6 tens, so the answer is 42 tens: 60 × 7 = 420.

items.q: You know that 8 × 3 = 24. What is 8 × 300?
items.e: Use the fact 8 × 3. 300 is 3 hundreds, so the answer is 24 hundreds: 8 × 300 = 2,400.

items.q: You know that 9 × 4 = 36. What is 9 × 40?
items.e: Use the fact 9 × 4. 40 is 4 tens, so the answer is 36 tens: 9 × 40 = 360.

items.q: You know that 12 × 5 = 60. What is 12 × 50?
items.e: Use the fact 12 × 5. 50 is 5 tens, so the answer is 60 tens: 12 × 50 = 600.

items.q: What is 70 × 8?
items.e: 7 × 8 = 56. 70 is 7 tens, so 70 × 8 = 56 tens = 560. (78 comes from adding.)

items.q: You know that 42 ÷ 7 = 6. What is 420 ÷ 7?
items.e: 420 is 42 tens. 42 tens ÷ 7 = 6 tens = 60. Check: 60 × 7 = 420.

items.q: What is 360 ÷ 9?
What is 480 ÷ 6?
You know that 27 ÷ 9 = 3. What is 2,700 ÷ 9?
items.e: 2,700 is 27 hundreds. 27 hundreds ÷ 9 = 3 hundreds = 300. Check: 300 × 9 = 2,700.

items.q: Find the missing number: ? × 8 = 560
items.e: 7 × 8 = 56, and 560 is 56 tens. So the missing number is 7 tens = 70. Check: 70 × 8 = 560.

items.q: Find the missing number: 30 × ? = 270
items.e: 30 is 3 tens and 270 is 27 tens. 3 × 9 = 27, so the missing number is 9. Check: 30 × 9 = 270.

items.q: Find the missing number: 400 ÷ ? = 80
items.e: 8 × 5 = 40, so 80 × 5 = 400. The missing number is 5. Check: 400 ÷ 5 = 80.

items.q: Which fact helps you work out 50 × 9?
Which fact helps you work out 630 ÷ 7?

sets.title: Multiply three numbers and change the order

items.q: What is 2 × 7 × 5?
items.e: Change the order to make 10 first: 2 × 5 = 10. Then 10 × 7 = 70.

items.q: What is 5 × 6 × 2?
items.e: Change the order to make 10 first: 5 × 2 = 10. Then 10 × 6 = 60.

items.q: What is 2 × 9 × 5?
items.e: Change the order to make 10 first: 2 × 5 = 10. Then 10 × 9 = 90.

items.q: What is 4 × 9 × 5?
items.e: Change the order to make 20 first: 4 × 5 = 20. Then 20 × 9 = 180. Remember to use all three numbers.

items.q: What is 2 × 6 × 7?
items.e: 2 × 6 = 12. Then 12 × 7 = 84. Remember to use all three numbers.

items.q: What is 4 × 5 × 6?
items.e: 4 × 5 = 20. Then 20 × 6 = 120. Or 4 × 6 = 24 first, then 24 × 5 = 120. Remember to use all three numbers.

items.q: To work out 2 × 13 × 5 in your head, which should you do first?
items.e: 2 × 5 = 10, a round number. Then 10 × 13 = 130 is easy. You may multiply the numbers in any order.

items.q: To work out 5 × 8 × 2 in your head, which should you do first?
items.e: 5 × 2 = 10, a round number. Then 10 × 8 = 80 is easy. You may multiply the numbers in any order.

items.q: To work out 4 × 7 × 5 in your head, which should you do first?
items.e: 4 × 5 = 20, a round number. Then 20 × 7 = 140 is easy. You may multiply the numbers in any order.

items.q: To work out 5 × 3 × 4 in your head, which should you do first?
items.e: 5 × 4 = 20, a round number. Then 20 × 3 = 60 is easy. You may multiply the numbers in any order.

items.q: Find the missing number: 9 × ? = 4 × 9
items.e: The same two numbers in a different order give the same answer: 9 × 4 = 4 × 9 = 36.

items.q: Find the missing number: 7 × 12 = 12 × ?
items.e: Swap the order: 7 × 12 = 12 × 7 = 84.

items.q: Find the missing number: ? × 6 = 6 × 11
items.e: Swap the order: 11 × 6 = 6 × 11 = 66.

items.q: Find the missing number: 8 × 3 × 5 = 5 × 3 × ?
items.e: Both sides must use the same three numbers: 8, 3 and 5. Both equal 120.

items.q: Find the missing number: 3 × 4 × 5 = 12 × ?
items.e: 3 × 4 = 12, and the 5 is still to be multiplied: 12 × 5 = 60.

items.q: Find the missing number: 4 × 5 × 7 = ? × 7
Find the missing number: 6 × 2 × 5 = 6 × ?
Which has the same answer as 4 × 3 × 5?
items.e: 4 × 5 = 20, so 4 × 3 × 5 = 20 × 3 = 60. 12 + 5 forgets to multiply by 5, and 4 × 8 adds 3 + 5.

items.q: Which has the same answer as 7 × 6 × 2?
Which is true?
items.e: You can swap the numbers in a multiplication: 9 × 4 = 4 × 9 = 36. This does not work for − or ÷.

items.q: 24 counters are in 3 equal rows. Find the missing factor: 3 × ? = 24
items.e: Count the counters in one row: 8. 3 × 8 = 24, so 3 and 8 are a factor pair of 24.
Count the counters in one row: 9. 4 × 9 = 36, so 4 and 9 are a factor pair of 36.

items.q: 18 counters are in 2 equal rows. Find the missing factor: 2 × ? = 18
items.e: Count the counters in one row: 9. 2 × 9 = 18, so 2 and 9 are a factor pair of 18.

items.q: 30 counters are in 5 equal rows. Find the missing factor: 5 × ? = 30
items.e: Count the counters in one row: 6. 5 × 6 = 30, so 5 and 6 are a factor pair of 30.

items.q: Which is a factor pair of 36?
items.e: 4 × 9 = 36. 16 + 20 also makes 36, but a factor pair must multiply to make 36.

items.q: Which is a factor pair of 40?
items.e: 5 × 8 = 40. 20 + 20 also makes 40, but a factor pair must multiply to make 40.

items.q: Which is a factor pair of 56?
items.e: 7 × 8 = 56. 50 + 6 also makes 56, but a factor pair must multiply to make 56.

items.q: Which is not a factor pair of 24?
items.e: 6 × 3 = 18, not 24. The others are factor pairs: 1 × 24 = 24, 2 × 12 = 24, 3 × 8 = 24.

items.q: Which is not a factor pair of 36?
items.e: 8 × 4 = 32, not 36. The others are factor pairs: 2 × 18 = 36, 3 × 12 = 36, 4 × 9 = 36.

items.q: Which is not a factor pair of 48?
items.e: 6 × 9 = 54, not 48. The others are factor pairs: 6 × 8 = 48, 4 × 12 = 48, 3 × 16 = 48.

items.q: Arjun lists the factor pairs of 24: 1 × 24, 2 × 12, 4 × 6. Which pair did he miss?
items.e: Test 1, 2, 3, 4 … in order. 3 × 8 = 24 is missing. Swapping a pair (like 6 × 4) does not make a new pair.

items.q: Amelia lists the factor pairs of 30: 1 × 30, 2 × 15, 5 × 6. Which pair did she miss?
items.e: Test 1, 2, 3, 4 … in order. 3 × 10 = 30 is missing. Swapping a pair (like 6 × 5) does not make a new pair.

items.q: Charlie lists the factor pairs of 36: 1 × 36, 2 × 18, 3 × 12, 6 × 6. Which pair did he miss?
items.e: Test 1, 2, 3, 4 … in order. 4 × 9 = 36 is missing. Swapping a pair (like 12 × 3) does not make a new pair.

items.q: How many factor pairs does 18 have?
items.e: 1 × 18, 2 × 9, 3 × 6. That is 3 pairs. 1 × 18 counts too.

items.q: How many factor pairs does 16 have?
items.e: 1 × 16, 2 × 8, 4 × 4. That is 3 pairs. Count 4 × 4 only once.

items.q: Use the factor pair 12 = 6 × 2. What is 12 × 5?
items.e: 12 × 5 = 6 × 2 × 5 = 6 × 10 = 60. Remember to use every factor.

items.q: Use the factor pair 14 = 7 × 2. What is 14 × 5?
items.e: 14 × 5 = 7 × 2 × 5 = 7 × 10 = 70. Remember to use every factor.

items.q: Use the factor pair 6 = 2 × 3. What is 15 × 6?
items.e: 15 × 6 = 15 × 2 × 3 = 30 × 3 = 90. Remember to use every factor.

items.q: Use the factor pair 8 = 4 × 2. What is 25 × 8?
items.e: 25 × 8 = 25 × 4 × 2 = 100 × 2 = 200. Remember to use every factor.

items.q: Which calculation helps you work out 16 × 5?
items.e: 8 × 2 = 16, so 16 × 5 = 8 × 2 × 5 = 8 × 10 = 80. Splitting 16 into its digits does not work: 1 × 6 = 6, not 16. And 8 × 8 = 64, not 16.

items.q: A box holds 10 packs of biscuits. Each pack has 8 biscuits. How many biscuits are in 3 boxes?
items.e: 3 × 10 × 8. Do 3 × 8 = 24 first, then 24 × 10 = 240 biscuits. 80 is only one box.

items.q: The school hall has 3 rows of 4 tables. Each table has 5 chairs. How many chairs are there?
items.e: 3 × 4 = 12 tables. 12 × 5 = 60 chairs. 12 is the number of tables, not chairs.

items.q: A pencil costs 30p. Ethan buys 8 pencils. How much does he spend?
In a game, every red card scores 0 points. Lily picks 9 red cards. How many points does she score?
items.e: 9 × 0 = 0. Nine lots of nothing is still nothing.

items.q: There are 28 pupils in Year 4. Each pupil gets 1 carton of milk. How many cartons are needed?
items.e: 28 × 1 = 28 cartons. Multiplying by 1 keeps the number the same.

items.q: The school orders 7 boxes of pencils. Each box has 30 pencils. How many pencils is that?
240 pupils go on a school trip. Each coach takes 40 pupils. How many coaches are needed?
A garden has 5 flower beds. Each bed has 4 rows of 6 plants. How many plants are there?
items.e: 4 × 6 = 24 plants in one bed. 24 × 5 = 120. Or 4 × 5 = 20 first, then 20 × 6 = 120.

items.q: Noah puts 24 chairs in equal rows with none left over. Which number of rows will not work?
items.e: 5 is not a factor of 24: 5 × 4 = 20 and 5 × 5 = 25. The others work: 3 × 8, 4 × 6 and 6 × 4 all make 24.

items.q: Evie puts 36 cupcakes on a tray in equal rows. Which could the tray show?
Raffle tickets cost 5p each. 4 children each buy 7 tickets. How much do they spend altogether?
items.e: 4 × 7 × 5. Do 4 × 5 = 20 first, then 20 × 7 = 140p = £1.40. 28p forgets the cost of each ticket.

items.q: Aisha has 7 bags of 9 sweets. George has 9 bags of 7 sweets. Who has more sweets?
items.e: 7 × 9 = 63 and 9 × 7 = 63. Swapping the order does not change the answer. (16 comes from adding.)

items.q: A PE teacher puts 350 cones into 7 equal stacks. How many cones are in each stack?
One lap of the field is 400 m. Oliver runs 3 laps. How far does he run?
A tray holds 15 eggs. How many eggs are on 4 trays?
Mohammed saves 20p every day for 9 days. How much does he save?
A packet of biscuits costs 25p. How much do 4 packets cost?
A car park has 8 rows. Each row has 30 spaces. How many spaces are there?
6 bags of crisps cost £3.60 altogether. Each bag costs the same. How much is one bag?
Zara buys 2 packs of pens every week for 5 weeks. Each pack has 6 pens. How many pens does she buy?
items.e: 2 × 6 × 5. Do 2 × 5 = 10 first, then 10 × 6 = 60 pens. 12 is only one week.
